exposure: Maternal nutrient restriction (60% vs 100% net energy requirements)
outcome: Microscopic placentome vascular density (percent capillary area and perimeter)
cohort: Twelve pregnant heifers (6 Angus and 6 Brahman) were assigned to either a control or total nutrient-restricted diet.
finding: Maternal nutrient restriction led to reduced ipsilateral uterine artery blood flow but compensatory increases in macroscopic and microscopic placentome blood vessel density, with Brahman heifers also showing a greater macroscopic density of cotyledonary blood vessels compared to Angus heifers.
